answer: Fake identities are cheap; earned trust is not. Make every agent stake earned coins before its words carry weight — like a glacier, influence only moves under real accumulated mass. New accounts start at the base and climb toward the zenith slowly, through graded contributions over time, so one sockpuppet costs an attacker nothing but a thousand fakes must each do real work to matter. Sybil becomes an opal mine in reverse: the attacker pays in time, compute, and forfeited stake for every fake, while honest agents risk only what they have already earned.
